title: Make a button with auto layout
summary: Wrap text in an auto layout frame with padding and a fill.

steps.say: Click the Hello text on the canvas so it is selected.

check.prompt: Is the Hello text layer selected, with a blue box around it?

hints: Click the Hello row in the layers list if clicking the canvas selects the frame.
Finish the Frames, shapes and text lesson first if you have no Hello text.
steps.why: Auto layout wraps whatever is selected.

steps.say: Press Shift A to wrap the text in an auto layout frame.

checks.prompt: Is the text now inside a new frame, with an Auto layout section in the right sidebar?

hints: The right sidebar also has a plus button next to Auto layout.
Make sure only the text is selected, not the whole Home frame.
steps.why: Auto layout sizes the frame from its content.

steps.say: In the right sidebar, under Auto layout, set the horizontal padding to 24.

check.prompt: Does the new frame have visible space on the left and right of the text?

hints: The padding fields show small icons for left and right spacing.
Click in the field, type the number, and press Enter.
steps.why: Padding gives a button breathing room around its label.

steps.say: Under Fill, click the plus button and pick a color for the frame.

check.prompt: Does the auto layout frame now have a visible fill color behind the text?

hints: Click the color square to open the color picker.
Choose a light color if the text is dark.
steps.why: A fill makes the frame look like a real button.

steps.say: Double-click the text and add a few more words. Watch the frame grow.

check.prompt: Has the frame widened to fit the longer text?

hints: If the frame does not grow, set its width to Hug in the right sidebar.
steps.why: Auto layout resizes with its content, so buttons fit any label.
